idiom_name: ES module of async service functions + a withTransaction helper over the driver
implementation_notes: The service class disappears into a module: services/order.js exports one async function per application operation, closing over a pool, and the transaction boundary is a small withTransaction(pool, fn) helper that checks out a single client, issues BEGIN, COMMIT or ROLLBACK and always releases the client - node-postgres deliberately provides no higher-level transaction abstraction, so this helper is written once and reused. There is no container, so wiring is plain module or factory arguments. The explicit structure is still justified when several entry points (HTTP routes, queue consumers, CLI) call the same operations; for a single route, calling the repository directly is simpler.
pitfalls: Never use pool.query inside a transaction: each call may run on a different pooled client, so the BEGIN/COMMIT pair guards nothing.
Forgetting client.release() in the finally block leaks pooled connections until every acquire blocks or times out.
A failed statement leaves the client in the aborted-transaction state ('E') until ROLLBACK runs; reusing that connection without rolling back fails every later query.
